body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.52 (naive base rate 0.55) that: Bajaj Consumer Care FY27 consolidated revenue from operations grows ≥17.0% YoY ("high teens" guide). Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (15-Oct-2026): H1 revenue ₹674 cr (+28%), H1 EBITDA ₹167 cr (+85%), Q2 EBITDA margin 25%; Almond Drops double-digit unit volume growth; GT and organized trade both 'mid-20s' growth. MD Naveen Pandey: 'for the year, we are expecting a high teens' growth. Gross margin 59.9% (West Asia war, edible-oil inflation); ~5% consumer price increase in Q3 (2–3% frontal + ml-age cut). Screener: FY26 sales ₹1,165 cr; quarterly sales Q3 FY26 306 (+31%), Q4 FY26 327 (+30%), Q1 FY27 342, Q2 FY27 333. Reasoning: H1 at +28% makes a high-teens year look easy, but the H2 base is hard (H2 FY26 grew ~30%), so ≥17% needs H2 growth of ~+10% while the company takes price and cuts ml-age into an inflationary rural market. Management's own 'high teens' (not 'mid-20s') signals they expect H2 to slow sharply. We sit fractionally below base. Resolution: YES if Bajaj Consumer Care's FY27 consolidated revenue from operations ÷ FY26 consolidated revenue from operations − 1 ≥ 17.0% (company's own reported growth figure if stated; else from the audited results; screener.in annual table as fallback). Source: Bajaj Consumer Care Q4 FY27 results / investor presentation (NSE); screener.in. Resolve by 2027-05-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Small-cap FMCG companies restating a full-year growth range at H1 with H1 well above it meet the range's lower part roughly 55% of the time when the H2 comparison base is much tougher.
